final_answer: Imagine a small town where every time the ice cream truck arrives, a nearby park sees a spike in people playing soccer. At first, someone might think the ice cream truck *causes* people to play soccer. But what if the real reason is that the ice cream truck only comes on sunny days, and on sunny days, more people are inclined to go to the park and play soccer? The ice cream truck and soccer games are correlated, but neither causes the other. The real cause is the sunny weather. This shows that just because two things happen together, it doesn’t mean one causes the other—there might be a hidden factor at play.
